ORDIN ANCE NO. 016-138 AN ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING AN INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGREEMENT WITH THE CITY OF CHICAGO TO RECEIVE TRANSIT TAX INCREMENT FINANCING (TIF) REVENUES AND THE IMPLEMENTATION OF VARIOUS ELEMENTS OF THE PLAN OF FINANCE FOR THE RED AND PURPLE MODERNIZATION PHASE ONE PROJECT 

WHEREAS, the Chicago Transit Authority (the “Authority”) is a political subdivision, body politic and municipal corporation of the State of Illinois organized and existing under the Metropolitan Transit Authority Act, 70 ILCS 3605 (the “MTA Act”); and 

WHEREAS, the Authority is undertaking the Red and Purple Modernization Program (“RPM”), the largest capital improvement project ever undertaken by the Authority, which will completely rebuild the nearly century old North Red Line from Belmont to Howard and the Purple Line from Belmont to Linden in Wilmette; and 

WHEREAS, the RPM will result in adding much needed capacity in a fast-growing residential corridor to accommodate current and future riders, and the delivery of faster and smoother rides, with less crowding and more frequent service; and 

WHEREAS, the RPM is scheduled to be completed in phases, which allows the Authority to make the greatest number of improvements while minimizing impacts on riders and the surrounding communities; and 

WHEREAS, the Red and Purple Modernization Program Phase One Project (the “Project”) consists generally of the following transportation improvements: (a) modernization, expansion and addition of Americans with Disabilities Act (“ADA”) accessibility at four Red Line stations (Lawrence, Argyle, Berwyn, and Bryn Mawr), (b) reconstruction and expansion of tracks, structures and viaducts to accommodate expanded stations and platforms from Leland Avenue on the south to near Ardmore Avenue on the north; (c) construction of a fifth track bypass for the Brown Line at the Clark junction, just north of Belmont station, (d) reconstruction and modernization of tracks, structures and viaducts to straighten curves and improve operating speeds from approximately School Street to near Cornelia Street, (e) upgrades of the Broadway power substation; (f) installation of a new higher-capacity signal system from approximately Belmont Avenue to Howard Street; (g) all associated systems infrastructure replacement, such as communication and traction power; and (h) acquisition of certain property that was previously authorized in Ordinance No.015-117 and Ordinance No. 016-026 as necessary or desirable for the construction and operation of aspects of the Project described in (a) through (g) above; and 2

WHEREAS, the Project will be accomplished by the Authority’s implementation of a plan of finance (the “RPM Plan of Finance”) as briefly described further below; and 

WHEREAS, the Authority is negotiating a full funding grant agreement (“the FFGA”) with the Federal Transit Administration (“FTA”) through its Capital Investment Grant Program for core capacity projects, and an FFGA as authorized by the Federal Transit Act is designed to provide a commitment of federal financial funding through the FTA for major capital investment transit projects and such an agreement establishes the terms and conditions of federal financial assistance for a project, covers the time period to complete the project, and facilitates timely and efficient management of the project in accordance with Federal law; and 

WHEREAS, the Authority is seeking approximately $957 million in federal financial assistance for the Project through the negotiation and execution of an FFGA, which FFGA will also also provide assurance and predictability to the Authority of Federal financial support for the Project; and; 

WHEREAS, Staff recommends that the FFGA negotiated between the FTA and the Authority be executed; and 

WHEREAS, to obtain the FFGA, the Authority has to provide the FTA with a comprehensive plan of finance showing the remaining commitments for the entirety of the Project costs (the “RPM Plan of Finance“), the additional elements of which are briefly described below and more fully in the body of this Ordinance; and 

WHEREAS, the RPM Plan of Finance will be implemented in phases over the next several years and it is in the best interest of the Authority for all the elements of the RPM Plan of Finance not previously authorized (or, in the case of the 2017 Sales Tax Bonds, to be authorized pursuant to a separate ordinance) to be authorized and approved pursuant to this Ordinance; and 

WHEREAS, the first additional element of the RPM Plan of Finance is aCongestion Mitigation and Air Quality Improvement grant, the program funding for which is allocated by the United States Department of Transportation (“USDOT”) on a regional basis and administered by the region’s Metropolitan Planning Organization (“MPO”) and the Chicago-area MPO is the Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning (CMAP) which in its 2016-2020 CMAQ program awarded the Authority a grant for the Project in the approximate amount of $125,000,000 (the “CMAQ Grant”) ; and 

WHEREAS, it is recommended that authority be given to negotiate and execute the CMAQ Grant; and 3

WHEREAS, the second additional element of the RPM Plan of Finance is (a) a loan (the “TIFIA Loan”) from the USDOT under the the Transportation Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act in an amount not to exceed $622,000,000; or (b) in lieu of the TIFIA Loan, Authority Sales Tax bonds or note(s) in a principal amount not to exceed $622,000,000 (the “IGA Sales Tax Bonds”) which in either case are expected to be repaid by incremental property tax revenues (“Transit TIF Revenues”) to be received from the City of Chicago (the “City”) generated from a tax increment financing redevelopment project area, located within a transit facility improvement area, to be established by the City, pursuant to the Tax Increment Allocation Redevelopment Act (65 ILCS 5/11-74.4-1 et seq), and in accordance with the terms of the Redevelopment and Intergovernmental Agreement between the City and the Authority (the “IGA”) (attached hereto as Exhibit A) (with repayment of both the TIFIA Loan and the IGA Sales Tax Bonds being secured by specified revenues sources as described below); and Staff is recommending that the Chicago Transit Board (the “Board”) approve the negotiation and execution of a TIFIA Loan in an amount not to exceed $622,000,000 or in lieu of the TIFIA Loan, the IGA Sales Tax Bonds, and the IGA (which IGA is intended to occur on or before November 30, 2016); and 

WHEREAS, the third additional element of the RPM Plan of Finance is $10,000,000 of revenues received from a previously authorized and currently effective (as amended) Intergovernmental Agreement between the City and the Authority for the City’s Bryn Mawr/Broadway Redevelopment Project Area previously approved by Ordinance No. 012-166 as amended in Ordinance No. 016-103; and 

WHEREAS, the fourth additional element of the RPM Plan of Finance are future RPM Sales Tax Bonds (as described below) in an aggregate amount not to exceed $350,000,000; and 

WHEREAS, the IGA Sales Tax Bonds and the RPM Sales Tax Bonds are collectively defined as the “Future Sales Tax Bonds”; and 

WHEREAS, the fifth additional element of the RPM Plan of Finance are proceeds $44,000,000 of Authority Sales Tax Bonds to be authorized pursuant to a separate ordinance and generally referred to as the 2017 Second Lien Sales Tax Bonds; and 

WHEREAS, given the duration and comprehensive nature of the RPM Plan of Finance, it is appropriate and in the best interests of the Authority for the President or designees to report annually to the Board on the status of implementation of the RPM Plan of Finance; and 

WHEREAS, repayment of the TIFIA Loan will be made through issuance and payment by the Authority of the RPM TIFIA Bonds (as described below); and 4

WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 12 of the MTA Act, the Authority has the continuing power to borrow money for the purpose of acquiring, constructing, reconstructing, extending or improving its Transportation System and to evidence its obligation to repay any money borrowed by issuing its revenue bonds payable solely from the revenues, or income or other funds, which the Authority may receive, and also has the power to issue its revenue bonds to refund any bonds at maturity or pursuant to redemption provisions; and 

WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 13 of the Local Government Debt Reform Act, 30 ILCS 350 (the “Local Government Debt Reform Act”), the Authority may pledge, as security for the payment of its bonds and other obligations, moneys deposited or to be deposited in any special fund of the Authority; and 

WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 6 of the Local Government Debt Reform Act, the Authority may include in the authorized amount of secured obligations and pay from the proceeds of the secured obligations an amount to provide for the payment of expenses of issuing the secured obligations including underwriter’s spread, and financial advisor and trustee fees; and 

WHEREAS, pursuant to and in accordance with the provisions of the MTA Act and the Local Government Debt Reform Act, the Authority previously authorized the execution and delivery of an Amended and Restated Master Trust Indenturedated as of April 1, 2014 securing Chicago Transit Authority Fare Box Receipts Revenue Bonds and Other Obligations (the “TIFIA Master Trust Indenture"), between the Authority and U.S. Bank National Association, Chicago, Illinois, as trustee ("TIFIA Trustee"), to provide for the issuance from time to time, after obtaining all necessary Board approvals, of bonds and other obligations secured by Farebox Pledged Revenues; and 

WHEREAS, in connection with the closing of the TIFIA Loan, the Authority will issue limited obligations (the “RPM TIFIA Bonds’) that constitute Senior Payment Obligations under the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture, with the principal of and interest on the RPM TIFIA Bonds secured by Farebox Pledged Revenues (as defined as “Pledged Revenues” in the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture) deposited into the Farebox Pledged Revenues Account; and 

WHEREAS, any RPM TIFIA Bonds are expected to be repaid from Transit TIF Revenues, although such RPM TIFIA Bonds would be secured only by Farebox Pledged Revenues in accordance with the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture; and 

WHEREAS, the Authority anticipates the receipt from time to time from the Regional Transportation Authority (the “RTA”) of amounts representing the Authority’s share (in accordance with the Regional Transportation Authority Act, 70 ILCS 3615 et seq. (the “RTA Act”), including Section 4.03.3 thereof) of (i) the tax receipts derived from 5

taxes imposed by the RTA pursuant to the RTA Act; (ii) amounts paid to the RTA by the State of Illinois (the “State”) from transfers to (a) the Regional Transportation Authority Occupation and Use Tax Replacement Fund, (b) the Public Transportation Fund, and (c) the RTA tax fund created by Section 4.03(n) of the RTA Act from the County and Mass Transit District Fund; and (iii) funds derived by RTA from any other source designated by law as a replacement source of funds for all or a portion of the RTA tax receipts described in clause (i), or the State payments described in clause (ii) (collectively, the “Sales Tax Receipts”); and 

WHEREAS, pursuant to a Trust Indenture dated July 1, 2008 by and between the Authority and U.S. Bank National Association, as trustee (the “2008 Trustee”), securing Chicago Transit Authority Sales and Transfer Tax Receipts Revenue Bonds, as supplemented (the “2008 Indenture”), the Authority has established and maintains the Sales Tax Receipts Fund held by the Authority and established in Section 504 of the 2008 Indenture; and 

WHEREAS, pursuant to a Trust Indenture dated March 1, 2010 by and between the Authority and U.S. Bank National Association, as trustee (the “2010 Trustee”), securing Chicago Transit Authority Sales Tax Receipts Revenue Bonds, as supplemented (the “2010 Indenture”), the Authority may issue, from time to time, Corporate Purpose Debt Obligations (as defined in the 2010 Indenture), after obtaining all necessary Board approvals, of other parity obligations secured by a pledge of the Sales Tax Receipts Fund granted by the 2008 Indenture and as provided in the 2010 Indenture; and 

WHEREAS, the Authority intends to authorize, pursuant to a separate ordinance, a Trust Indenture by and between the Authority and Zions Bank, a division of ZB, National Association, as trustee (the “2017 Trustee”), securing Chicago Transit Authority Second Lien Sales Tax Receipts Revenue Bonds, as supplemented (the “2017 Indenture”), pursuant to which the Authority may issue, from time to time, Second Lien Obligations (as defined in the 2017 Indenture), after obtaining all necessary Board approvals, of other obligations secured by a subordinate pledge of the Sales Tax Receipts Fund granted by the 2008 Indenture and 2010 Indenture and as provided in the 2017 Indenture; and 

WHEREAS, pursuant to and in accordance with the provisions of the Act, the Local Government Debt Reform Act, the 2010 Indenture and the 2017 Indenture, as applicable, the Authority now desires to authorize the execution and delivery of one or more supplemental indentures (the “Sales Tax Supplemental Indentures”) between the Authority and the 2010 Trustee or the 2017 Trustee, as applicable, to provide for the issuance of one or more series of its Future Sales Tax Bonds as additional bonds, or refunding bonds, or both, under the 2010 Indenture or the 2017 Indenture, as applicable, which Future Sales Tax Bonds may be issued at one time or from time to 6

time and in one or more series, and shall be secured by the Sales Tax Receipts and income from the temporary investment thereof, as provided in the 2010 Indenture or the 2017 Indenture, as applicable, with the proceeds of the Future Sales Tax Bonds to be used to finance a portion of the costs of the Project; and 

WHEREAS, if and to the extent issued, the IGA Sales Tax Bonds are expected to be repaid from Transit TIF Revenues, although such IGA Sales Tax Bonds would be secured only by Sales Tax Receipts in accordance with the 2010 Indenture or the 2017 Indenture, as applicable; and 

WHEREAS, the Future Sales Tax Bonds are limited obligations of the Authority payable from the Sales Tax Receipts and moneys, securities and funds pledged to the payment of the Sales Tax Bonds under the 2010 Indenture or the 2017 Indenture, as applicable, and the Future Sales Tax Bonds are not, and shall not be or become, an indebtedness or obligation of the State or any political subdivision of the State (other than the Authority) or of any municipality within the State, nor shall any Future Sales Tax Bond be or become an indebtedness of the Authority within the purview of any constitutional limitation or provision; and 

WHEREAS, the Future Sales Tax Bonds may be issued in one or more series, including refunding Sales Tax Bonds issued to refinance Sales Tax Bonds initially issued as bond anticipation notes or other shorter term instruments pursuant to this Ordinance; and 

WHEREAS, the Future Sales Tax Bonds may be issued as bonds bearing interest at variable rates or fixed rates as set forth in the Indenture, and the Authorized Officers may, from time to time, change interest modes on Future Sales Tax Bonds bearing interest at variable rates (“Variable Rate Sales Tax Bonds”); and 

WHEREAS, In anticipation of the issuance of the Future Sales Tax Bonds, the Board desires to authorize and direct any of the Authorized Officers to act on behalf of the Board and the Authority to take certain actions necessary to permit the Authority to offer the proposed Future Sales Tax Bonds for sale pursuant to the Preliminary Official Statements, as defined herein, and take all other necessary actions relating to the offer, sale and delivery of the Future Sales Tax Bonds; and 

WHEREAS, the Authority desires to authorize the procurement of one or more policies of bond insurance with respect to all or a portion of Future Sales Tax Bonds if determined to be desirable in connection with the sale of the Future Sales Tax Bonds; and 7

WHEREAS, The Authority desires to authorize the procurement of one or more Credit Facilities (as defined herein) in connection with the sale of the Future Sales Tax Bonds; and 

WHEREAS, in anticipation of the negotiation of the TIFIA Loan, the issuance of the RPM TIFIA Bonds, the issuance of the Future Sales Tax Bonds, the execution of the FFGA, the execution of the CMAQ Grant and the execution of the IGA, the Authority desires to authorize and direct any of its Authorized Officers (as defined in Section 1 of this Ordinance) to perform specific acts or duties hereunder by ordinance duly adopted by the Authority; and 

WHEREAS, the Authority has satisfied all conditions, or, in the event that the time for the performance of any such condition has not yet occurred, will satisfy all such conditions, stated in the MTA Act, the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture, the 2010 Indenture and the 2017 Indenture, as applicable, as prerequisites to the issuance of the RPM TIFIA Bonds and the Future Sales Tax Bonds; and 

WHEREAS, the Authority has caused to be prepared and presented to the Board certain documents and instruments referred to in this Ordinance relating to the implementation of the RPM Plan of Finance and it appears that each of these documents or instruments is in appropriate form and is an appropriate document or instrument to be executed and delivered for the purposes intended; and 

WHEREAS, the Authority desires to finance all or a portion of the Project with proceeds of the Future Sales Tax Bonds or other obligations issued subsequent to the passage of this Ordinance (collectively “Debt Obligations”); and 

WHEREAS, the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the “Code”), authorizes the Authority to reimburse itself for capital expenditures that it made for capital improvements from the proceeds of such Debt Obligations, provided that certain requirements set forth in the Code are satisfied and the Authority recognizes that it may incur such expenditures with respect to the Project (the “Induced Expenditures”) prior to its receipt of the proceeds of any Debt Obligations; and 

WHEREAS, the Authority reasonably expects to reimburse all or a portion of any Induced Expenditures with the proceeds of the Debt Obligations; now therefore: 

BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CHICAGO TRANSIT BOARD 

OF THE CHICAGO TRANSIT AUTHORITY: 

SECTION 1. Definitions. In this ordinance, each of the terms defined in the above recitals shall have the meanings ascribed to such terms and the following terms 8

shall have the meanings ascribed to the terms below, unless the context otherwise requires: 

(a) “Authorized Officer” means the Chairman of the Board, the President or Treasurer of the Authority, the Treasurer/Chief Financial Officer, or any other officer or employee of the Authority or member of the Board authorized to perform specific acts or duties hereunder by ordinance duly adopted by the Authority. 

(b) Terms not defined herein shall have the meaning given thereto in the TIFIA Loan Agreement, the TIFIA Master Indenture, the 2008 Indenture, the 2010 Indenture or the 2017 Indenture, the RPM TIFIA Bonds, the FFGA, the CMAQ Grant or the IGA, as applicable. 

SECTION 2. Findings and Determinations. It is found and declared by the Board as follows: 

(a) All of the recitals contained in the preamble to this Ordinance are incorporated in full as part of this Ordinance. 

(b) In order to provide money for the Authority to pay for a portion of the costs associated with the Project, it is necessary and proper and in the best interests of the Authority and the public for the Authority to borrow money, in anticipation of Farebox Pledged Revenues, and as evidence of its obligation to repay such borrowings, to issue the RPM TIFIA Bonds in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed $622,000,000 plus accrued interest, pursuant to this Ordinance, and to use the proceeds to fund the costs associated with the Project. 

(c) In order to provide money for the Authority to pay for a portion of the costs associated with the Project, it is also necessary and proper and in the best interests of the Authority and the public for the Authority to borrow money, in anticipation of Sales Tax Receipts, and as evidence of its obligation to repay such borrowings, to issue the IGA Sales Tax Bonds in lieu of the RPM TIFIA Bonds referred to in subparagraph (b) above in an outstanding aggregate principal amount not to exceed $622,000,000 and the RPM Sales Tax Bonds in an outstanding aggregate principal amount not to exceed $350,000,000 (including, in each case, refunding Future Sales Tax Bonds issued to refinance Future Sales Tax Bonds initially issued as bond anticipation notes or other shorter term instruments pursuant to this Ordinance, and in each case plus accrued interest) and to use the proceeds to fund the costs associated with the Project. 

(d) The RPM TIFIA Bonds shall be issued under Section 12 of the MTA Act and shall constitute Senior Payment Obligations under the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture. 9

(e) Portions of the proceeds of the sale of the Future Sales Tax Bonds may be applied to finance the costs of the Project, to fund a deposit to a reserve fund established and maintained pursuant to the 2010 Indenture or the 2017 Indenture, to fund capitalized interest on the Future Sales Tax Bonds for a period not to exceed the greater of two years or six months following the completion of the Project to be financed with the proceeds of the Future Sales Tax Bonds, and to fund certain costs of issuance of the Future Sales Tax Bonds (including bond insurance premiums, costs associated with obtaining Credit Facilities and related costs). 

(f) The Authority’s ability to change interest modes on Variable Rate Bonds from time to time in various principal amounts will enhance the Authority’s opportunities to obtain financing with the most favorable terms available. 

(g) The fee allocation arrangement and level of fees to be paid to the financial advisors, bond insurer, rating agencies, trustees, co-bond counsel and for cost of issuance shall be as determined by the Treasurer of the Authority, provided such fees (exclusive of fees for bond insurance or debt service reserve policy) do not exceed for each issuance of RPM TIFIA Bonds and Future Sales Tax Bonds in the aggregate two percent (2%) of the principal amount of each such issuance and all such fees (exclusive of fees for bond insurance) shall be paid as part of the costs of issuance of such Bonds. The Authority is authorized to utilize funds of the Authority (other than the proceeds of the RPM TIFIA Bonds or the Future Sales Tax Bonds) to pay costs associated with the issuance of a bond insurance policy or debt service reserve policy. 

(h) Pursuant to Section 13 of the Local Government Debt Reform Act, amounts on deposit in the Sales Tax Receipts Fund held by the Authority and established in the 2008 Indenture (subject however to the provisions of the 2008 Indenture, the 2010 Indenture and the 2017 Indenture), to the extent and in the manner provided herein and in the 2010 Indenture and the 2017 Indenture, shall be and are hereby pledged as security for the payment of the Future Sales Tax Bonds. 

(i) Pursuant to Section 10 of the Local Government Debt Reform Act, the Board determines that the Future Sales Tax Bonds shall be sold by means of a private, negotiated sale to one or more investment banks as underwriters (the “Underwriters”) pursuant to the terms and provisions of one or more bond purchase agreements (each a “Bond Purchase Agreement”) and that the manner of sale will accommodate current market practices and will provide an opportunity to sell the Future Sales Tax Bonds under the most favorable terms. 

(j) Authority is hereby delegated to the Treasurer of the Authority (and if such Treasurer is not available, any other Authorized Officer): (i) to execute and deliver one or more Bond Purchase Agreements to sell the Furture Sales Tax Bonds to the Underwriters pursuant to the terms and conditions of such Bond Purchase Agreements, 10 

provided that the underwriting spread of the Underwriters shall not exceed 1% of the aggregate principal amount of the Future Sales Tax Bonds being sold at such time; (ii) to determine to change interest modes on all or part of any series of Variable Rate Bonds from time to time in accordance with the Indenture as and to the extent such officer determines is desirable and in the best financial interest of the Authority; (iii) determine the timing and amount of the principal amortization of Variable Rate Bonds, as and to the extent such officer determines from time to time that such principal amortization is desirable and in the best interest of the Authority; and (iv) determine to transfer, modify and/or terminate swap agreements and to pay such amounts in respect of such transfer, modification and/or termination, all as and to the extent that such officer determines it is desirable and in the best financial interest of the Authority. 

(k) The Board hereby determines that it is necessary and in the best interests of the Authority to delegate to the Authorized Officers the authority to determine various terms pertaining to the negotiation of the TIFIA Loan, the issuance and delivery of the RPM TIFIA Bonds, the issuance and sale of the Future Sales Tax Bonds, the execution of the FFGA, the execution of the CMAQ Grant and the execution of the IGA within the limitations set forth in the MTA Act and this Ordinance, and that such delegation is permissible. 

SECTION 3. Authorization of the RPM TIFIA Bonds. Pursuant to the MTA Act, the Local Government Debt Reform Act and the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture, the Authority hereby authorizes the issuance of the RPM TIFIA Bonds in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed $622,000,000, plus accrued interest, for the purposes set forth above. The RPM TIFIA Bonds shall mature not later than forty (40) years from the date of issuance of the RPM TIFIA Bonds and shall bear interest at a rate or rates not to exceed 6 and 1/2% per annum. The Authorized Officers are hereby granted the authority to approve on behalf of the Authority the final principal amount, maturity schedule, interest rate or rates, and capitalized interest, if any, with respect to the RPM TIFIA Bonds within the parameters set forth in this ordinance, and as provided in TIFIA Master Trust Indenture, the TIFIA Supplemental Indenture (as defined herein), and the RPM TIFIA Loan Agreement (as defined herein) and in the MTA Act, and as the Authorized Officer executing the same shall determine to be in the best financial interests of the Authority. 

SECTION 4. Certain Terms of the RPM TIFIA Bonds; Execution and Delivery of the RPM TIFIA Bonds. 

(a) The RPM TIFIA Bonds shall be designated as the Chicago Transit Authority TIFIA Bonds, with series designation as appropriate, and may be issued in one or more separate series with such additional designation as may be appropriate. The RPM TIFIA Bonds shall be in the denominations, dated, numbered and substantially in the form as provided in the RPM TIFIA Loan Agreement, and shall 11 

mature on the dates, shall be issued in the principal amounts, and shall bear interest payable at the times and at the rates per annum to be specified in the RPM TIFIA Loan Agreement. 

(b) The RPM TIFIA Bonds shall be executed by the manual or duly authorized facsimile signatures of the Chairman of the Board, the Treasurer of the Authority and the Secretary or Assistant Secretary of the Board and shall have the corporate seal of the Authority affixed to it (or a facsimile of that seal impressed, imprinted or otherwise reproduced thereon). The RPM TIFIA Bonds executed by the facsimile signature of the Chairman of the Board, the Treasurer of the Authority and the Secretary or Assistant Secretary of the Board shall be as effective as if executed by the hand of such officer. 

(c) The RPM TIFIA Bonds are limited obligations of the Authority, secured solely by Farebox Pledged Revenues. The RPM TIFIA Bonds are not, and shall not be or constitute an indebtedness of the RTA, the State, or of any other political subdivision of or municipality within the State, except the Authority. 

(d) The RPM TIFIA Bonds are subject to redemption prior to maturity. 

(e) The proceeds of the RPM TIFIA bonds are to be used to pay for costs associated with the Project, as described in the RPM TIFIA Loan Agreement (including the payment or redemption of any bonds or other obligations which may have been previously issued by the Authority to pay for costs associated with the Project). 

SECTION 5. Pledge of the Farebox Pledged Revenues Account to Secure the RPM TIFIA Bonds. The Authority shall establish a Farebox Pledged Revenues Account as a special fund of the Authority as part of the trust estate established by the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture. A Debt Service Account may be established under the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture for the RPM TIFIA Bonds and shall be a special fund of the Authority held in trust by the TIFIA Trustee as part of the trust estate under the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture. Subject to use and application in accordance with the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture and the TIFIA Supplemental Indenture, the Authority hereby pledges the following as security for the payment of the principal of and interest on the RPM TIFIA Bonds and shall be subject to the lien of the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture: 

(a) The Farebox Pledged Revenues Account (as defined as “Pledged Revenues Account” in the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture); 

(b) All moneys and securities and earnings thereon in all funds and accounts established and maintained pursuant to the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture; and 12 

(c) Any and all other moneys and securities furnished from time to time to the TIFIA Trustee by the Authority or on behalf of the Authority or by any other persons to be held by the TIFIA Trustee under the terms of the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture. 

SECTION 6. Application of the RPM TIFIA Bond Proceeds. All net proceeds received upon the issuance of the RPM TIFIA Bonds shall be paid to the Authority for deposit into the Construction Account (as defined in the RPM TIFIA Bonds Supplemental Indenture) or other account designated by the Authority and shall be applied in accordance with Section 12 of the MTA Act. 

SECTION 7. Approval of the RPM Supplemental Indenture. The Authorized Officers are hereby authorized to execute and deliver one or more supplemental indentures in connection with the RPM TIFIA Bonds (the “RPM Supplemental Indenture”) in the name and on behalf of the Authority in substantially the form of those supplemental indentures previsouly issued pursuant to the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture, with such other or further changes in the RPM Supplemental Indenture as may be approved by any Authorized Officer executing the same. The execution of the RPM Supplemental Indenture by any Authorized Officer shall constitute conclusive evidence of the approval by such Authorized Officer, the Authority and the Board of any and all such changes. 

SECTION 8. Approval of the RPM TIFIA Loan Agreement. The Authorized Officers are hereby authorized to execute and deliver the RPM TIFIA Loan Agreement in connection with the RPM TIFIA Loan in the name and on behalf of the Authority in substantially the form of those loan agreements previously executed and delivered by the Authority in connection with the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture (the “RPM TIFIA Loan Agreement”), with such other or further changes in the RPM TIFIA Loan Agreement as are specific to the Project, the RPM Plan of Finance, the IGA and the Transit TIF Revenues and as otherwise may be approved by any Authorized Officer executing the same. The execution of the RPM TIFIA Loan Agreement by any Authorized Officer shall constitute conclusive evidence of the approval by such Authorized Officer, the Authority and the Board of any and all such changes. 

SECTION 9. Continuing Appropriation of Farebox Pledged Revenues. This Ordinance shall constitute a continuing appropriation of all Farebox Pledged Revenues, which shall be used for the purposes specified in and permitted by the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture and the RPM Supplemental Indenture so long as the RPM TIFIA Bonds remain outstanding. 

SECTION 10. Costs and Expenses relating to the Issuance of the RPM TIFIA Bonds. The costs of issuance of the RPM TIFIA Bonds, including financial advisor, special counsel, bond counsel and trustee fees shall be paid from legally available funds of the Authority. 13 

SECTION 11. Appointment of TIFIA Trustee, Paying Agent and Registrar. U.S. Bank National Association is hereby appointed as TIFIA Trustee for the RPM TIFIA Bonds under the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture. The TIFIA Trustee shall accept and agree to the trusts created by the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture, including, without limitation, the duties and responsibilities of Paying Agent and Registrar (as such terms are defined in the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture). Additionally, the TIFIA Trustee shall hold in trust, invest and use amounts in funds and accounts created as provided by the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture with respect to the RPM TIFIA Bonds in accordance with Section 12 of the MTA Act for the benefit of the Authority and the protection of the owner of the RPM TIFIA Bonds. 

SECTION 12. Authorization of the Future Sales Tax Bonds for the Purposes Authorized by this Ordinance. Pursuant to Section 12 of the MTA Act and the Local Government Debt Reform Act, the Board hereby authorizes the issuance of the Future Sales Tax Bonds at one time or from time to time and in one or more series, as follows: the IGA Sales Tax Bonds in an outstanding aggregate principal amount not to exceed $622,000,000 in lieu of the RPM TIFIA Bonds and the RPM Sales Tax Bonds in an outstanding aggregate principal amount not to exceed $350,000,000 (including, in each case, refunding Future Sales Tax Bonds issued to refinance Future Sales Tax Bonds initially issued as bond anticipation notes or other shorter term instruments pursuant to this Ordinance, and in each case plus accrued interest). The proceeds of the Future Sales Tax Bonds shall be used for the purpose of financing a portion of the costs of the Project. 

SECTION 13. Certain Terms of the Future Sales Tax Bonds; Execution and Delivery of the Sales Tax Bonds. 

(a) The Chairman of the Board, the President, or such other Authorized Officer designated by the Chairman is authorized to execute the Future Sales Tax Bonds on behalf of the Authority, and the Assistant Secretary to the Board shall attest thereto, in each case by manual or facsimile signatures, and the seal (or a facsimile thereof) of the Authority shall be impressed, imprinted, engraved or otherwise reproduced thereon, and the Future Sales Tax Bonds shall be delivered to the 2010 Trustee under the 2010 Indenture or the 2017 Trustee under the 2017 Indenture, as applicable, for authentication and delivery to the Underwriters pursuant to the applicable Bond Purchase Agreement. 

(b) The Future Sales Tax Bonds shall be in the form and denominations set forth in the 2010 Indenture or the 2017 Indenture, as applicable, and the Sales Tax Supplemental Indenture, shall be dated no earlier than January 1, 2017, shall be numbered as provided in the Indenture, shall mature on the dates, shall be issued in the principal amounts and in the designated series, shall bear interest payable at the times and at the rates per annum and shall be subject to redemption prior to maturity upon the 14 

terms and conditions to be specified in the applicable Bond Purchase Agreement, the 2010 Indenture or the 2017 Indenture (as applicable) and the Official Statement (as defined in herein), subject to the limitations set forth in subsection (f) hereof. 

(c) The Future Sales Tax Bonds shall be designated “[IGA][RPM] Sales Tax Receipts Revenue Bonds, Series 20__” or [“IGA][RPM] Second Lien Sales Tax Receipts Revenue Bonds, Series 20__” (as applicable) and include such further appropriate designation as to series as is set forth in the Sales Tax Supplemental Indenture(s). The Future Sales Tax Bonds may be issued bearing interest at a fixed interest rate or rates or at variable interest rates (including but not limited to variable interest rates that are reset daily or weekly by a remarketing agent and variable interest rates commonly referred to as “flexible”, “adjustable,” “floating rate” and “commercial paper” (including under circumstances in which specified bonds of a series bear interest at rates that differ from the rates borne by other bonds of the series and have different accrual, mandatory tender and purchase provisions and default and remedy provisions) (herein collectively referred to as “Variable Rates”), as more fully set forth in the Indenture, but in no event shall such rate or rates (i) with respect to Future Sales Tax Bonds bearing interest at a fixed interest rate, exceed 10% per annum, and (ii) with respect to Variable Rate Bonds, exceed the greater of (A) 10% per annum and (B) the maximum interest rate permissible under Illinois law; provided, however, that so long as such Variable Rate Bonds are secured by a letter of credit, the maximum interest rate with respect to such Variable Rate Bonds shall be calculated pursuant to such letter of credit. Interest on the Future Sales Tax Bonds shall be payable on each interest payment date as provided in the Sales Tax Supplemental Indenture (as executed and delivered by the Authority). The Future Sales Tax Bonds may be issued under structures commonly referred to as “bond anticipation notes”, “medium term notes” or “put option bonds”, including with provisions for the mandatory tender and purchase of such Variable Rate Bonds prior to otherwise applicable maturity or mandatory redemption dates, the extension of any stated mandatory purchase requirements and an increase in the interest rate payable on such Variable Rate Bonds following any such extension; and may be secured as to principal, purchase price, redemption price and interest by one or more letters of credit. Any Sales Tax Bonds that initially bear interest at a Variable Rate may thereafter bear such other interest rate or rates as may be established in accordance with the provisions of the Sales Tax Supplemental Indenture as the Authorized Officer shall direct. Any Future Sales Tax Bonds that bear interest at a fixed rate may be issued as current interest bonds, as Capital Appreciation Bonds (as defined in subsection (d) below) or as Capital Appreciation Bonds that convert to current interest bonds at a future date after their issuance. 

(d) All or any portion of the Future Sales Tax Bonds may be issued as bonds payable in one payment on a fixed date ("Capital Appreciation Bonds”). Each series of Capital Appreciation Bonds shall be dated the date of issuance thereof and shall also bear the date of authentication, shall be in fully registered form, shall be numbered as 15 

determined by the applicable bond registrar and shall be in denominations equal to the original principal amounts of such Capital Appreciation Bonds or any integral multiple thereof, each such original principal amount representing Compound Accreted Value (as hereinafter defined) at maturity of such minimum amounts and integral multiples thereof as shall be agreed upon by an Authorized Officer and the purchasers of such Capital Appreciation Bonds (but no single Bond shall represent Compound Accreted Value maturing on more than one date). As used herein, the “Compound Accreted Value” of a Capital Appreciation Bond on any date of determination shall be an amount equal to the original principal amount (or integral multiple thereof) plus an investment return accrued to the date of such determination at a semiannual compounding rate which is necessary to produce the yield to maturity borne by such Capital Appreciation Bond. Any Capital Appreciation Bonds may contain provisions for the conversion of the Compound Accreted Value of such bonds into current interest rate bonds at such time following the initial issuance as shall be approved by an Authorized Officer. 

(e) All or any portion of the Future Sales Tax Bonds may be issued as (i) bonds on which the interest paid and received is excludable from the gross income of the owners thereof for federal income tax purposes under the Code (except to the extent that such interest is taken into account in computing an adjustment used in determining the alternative minimum tax for certain corporations); or (ii) bonds on which the interest paid and received is not excludable from the gross income of the owners thereof for federal income tax purposes under the Code (“Taxable Bonds”). Nothing contained in this Ordinance shall limit the ability of the Authority to issue all or a portion of the Future Sales Tax Bonds as Taxable Bonds if determined by an Authorized Officer to be in the best interest of the Authority. 

(f) The Future Sales Tax Bonds shall mature on such dates as provided in the applicable Sales Tax Supplemental Indenture, but in no event later than 40 years from the dated date of that Supplmental Indenture. The Future Sales Tax Bonds shall be subject to redemption as provided in the 2010 Indenture or the 2016 Indenture, as applicable. The Future Sales Tax Bonds may be redeemable prior to maturity at the option of the Authority, in whole or in part on any date, at such times and at such redemption prices not to exceed 103% of the principal amount of Future Sales Tax Bonds to be redeemed, as shall be determined by an Authorized Officer at the time of the sale thereof. The Future Sales Tax Bonds may be made subject to sinking fund redemption, at par plus accrued interest to the date fixed for redemption, as determined by an Authorized Officer at the time of the sale thereof. The Sales Tax Supplemental Indenture may provide for the establishment of a debt service reserve account if an Authorized Officer determines that the establishment of such a reserve would be advantageous to the Authority. 

(g) The Future Sales Tax Bonds are limited obligations of the Authority payable from the Sales Tax Receipts under the 2010 Indenture or the Available Sales 16 

Tax Receipts under the 2017 Indenture, as applicable, and the moneys, securities and funds pledged to the payment of the Future Sales Tax Bonds under the 2010 Indenture or the 2017 Indenture, as applicable, and the Future Sales Tax Bonds are not, and shall not be or constitute an indebtedness of the RTA, the State, or of any other political subdivision of or municipality within the State (other than the Authority). The Future Sales Tax Bonds shall not be secured by any lien upon any physical property of the Authority. An Authorized Officer may from time to time determine to make payments on the Future Sales Tax Bonds from other available funds, without a pledge of such funds under the 2010 Indenture or the 2017 Indenture, as applicable. 

SECTION 14. Pledge of Sales Tax Receipts Fund to Secure Parity Obligations. The Board hereby confirms the pledge by the Authority, as part of the trust estate established by the 2010 Indenture and the 2017 Indenture, as applicable, with respect to the Sales Tax Receipts Fund to the Future Sales Tax Bonds. 

SECTION 15. Approval of the Sales Tax Supplemental Indentures. To provide for the details of and to prescribe the terms and conditions upon which the Future Sales Tax Bonds are to be issued, secured, executed, authenticated and held, the Authorized Officers are each hereby authorized to execute and deliver the Sales Tax Supplemental Indentures and such other additional supplemental indentures as the Authorized Officers deem necessary or appropriate, in the name and on behalf of the Authority, in each case in substantially the form previously executed in connection with bonds issued pursuant to the 2010 Indenture and the 2017 Indenture, with such other or further changes in the Sales Tax Supplemental Indenture and any other supplemental indentures as may be approved by any Authorized Officer executing the same. The execution of the Sales Tax Supplemental Indenture and any other supplemental indentures by any Authorized Officer shall constitute conclusive evidence of the approval by such Authorized Officer and the Authority of any and all such changes from the form of the Sales Tax Supplemental Indenture presented to this meeting and approved hereby. 

SECTION 16. Approval of Use and Distribution of the Preliminary Official Statement. The Authorized Officers are each hereby authorized to use and distribute one or more Preliminary Official Statements for the Future Sales Tax Bonds in the form of Preliminary Official Statements previously utilized by and on behalf of the Authority in connection with bonds issued pursuant to the 2010 Indenture and the 2017 Indenture, which Preliminary Official Statement shall also include such information as shall be deemed necessary or appropriate by any Authorized Officer to approve such Preliminary Official Statement, including information concerning the Project, the RPM Plan of Finance, information concerning the bond insurer and bond insurance policy relating to the related Future Sales Tax Bonds, information conforming to the form of Indenture and such other information as such officer deems necessary or appropriate under the circumstances. Upon the determination of any Authorized Officer that the 17 

Preliminary Official Statement is deemed final, the Underwriters are hereby authorized to publish and distribute such Preliminary Official Statement for use, together with the Indenture including the form of the Sales Tax Supplemental Indenture or other applicable supplemental indentures, in connection with a public offering of the Future Sales Tax Bonds in an aggregate original principal amount within the parameters described herein. 

SECTION 17. Approval of the Bond Purchase Agreements. The Authorized Officers are each hereby authorized to execute and deliver one or more Bond Purchase Agreements in the name and on behalf of the Authority in substantially the form of bond purchase agreements previously executed and delivered in connection with bonds issued pursuant to the 2010 Indenture and the 2017 Indenture, with such changes as may be approved by the Authorized Officer executing the same, with such execution to constitute conclusive evidence of the approval of such Authorized Officer and the Authority of any and all such changes. 

SECTION 18. Approval of the Continuing Disclosure Undertakings. The Authorized Officers are each hereby authorized to execute and deliver one or more Continuing Disclosure Undertakings (each, a “Continuing Disclosure Undertaking”) in respect of the Future Sales Tax Bonds in the name and on behalf of the Authority in substantially the form previously executed by the Authority in connection with bonds issued under the 2010 Indenture and the 2017 Indenture, with such changes as may be approved by any Authorized Officer executing the same, with such execution to constitute conclusive evidence of the approval of such Authorized Officer and the Authority of any and all such changes. 

SECTION 19. Official Statements. The Authorized Officers are each hereby authorized to prepare, execute and distribute one or more final Official Statement (collectively, the “Official Statement”), which shall reflect the final terms and conditions of the Future Sales Tax Bonds as established in the related Bond Purchase Agreement, the 2010 Indenture or 2017 Indenture (as applicable, the Sales Tax Supplemental Indenture and other documents and instruments approved and authorized hereby. Such Official Statement shall be in the form of the Preliminary Official Statement deemed final by the Authority with such changes therein as shall be necessary to conform to this Ordinance and such other changes therein as shall be approved by any Authorized Officer executing the same, with such execution to constitute conclusive evidence of the approval of such Authorized Officer and the Authority of any and all such changes. 

SECTION 20. Authorization of the Purchase of Municipal Bond Insurance Policies. In connection with any sale of any series of the Future Sales Tax Bonds, any one of the Authorized Officers is authorized to obtain one or more policies of bond insurance from recognized bond insurers selected by such Authorized Officer. The Authorized Officer may, on behalf of the Authority, make covenants with such bond 18 

insurers as are necessary or desirable to obtain such policies, execute and deliver such documents and agreements and pay such related costs with Future Sales Tax Bond proceeds or with the funds of the Authority, as are necessary to carry out the purposes of this Ordinance. Any of the Authorized Officers is further authorized to request one or more of the financial advisors to solicit proposals from recognized bond insurers for one or more policies of bond insurance. The Board hereby determines that competitive bidding for such bond insurance is not required under Section 1.4B of the Chicago Transit Authority Procurement Policy and Procedures inasmuch as the services required are for a professional services, or require technical or artistic skill, and federal funds are not utilized and, as a result, any of the Authorized Officers is authorized to determine whether, under then current market conditions, it is most advantageous to the Authority to select one or more policies of insurance pursuant to a competitive process or a private negotiated process. If such Authorized Officer so determines that a negotiated process is most advantageous, any of the Authorized Officers is further authorized to select one or more of such policies of bond insurance based upon a determination of what is in the best interest of the Authority and, regardless of the manner of selection, to negotiate and execute all required agreements and certificates with such selected bond insurer(s), such agreements and certificates to be in a form acceptable to the General Counsel of the Authority. 

SECTION 21. Authorization of the Purchase of Debt Service Reserve Policys relating to the Sales Tax Bonds. Any one of the Authorized Officers is authorized to obtain one or more surety bonds or debt service reserve policies issued by a nationally recognized insurance provider (the “Surety Provider”) to satisfy any reserve requirement under the 2010 Indenture or the 2017 Indenture, as applicable. The Authorized Officer may, on behalf of the Authority, make covenants with such Surety Provider as are necessary or desirable to obtain such policies, execute and deliver such documents and agreements and pay such related costs with Sales Tax Bond proceeds or with funds of the Authority, as are necessary to carry out the purposes of this Ordinance. The Board hereby determines that competitive bidding for such policies is not required under Section 1.4B of the Chicago Transit Authority Procurement Policy and Procedures inasmuch as the services required are for a professional services, or require technical or artistic skill, and federal funds are not utilized and, as a result, any of the Authorized Officers is authorized to determine whether under then current market conditions it is most advantageous to the Authority, to select one or more policies pursuant to a competitive process or a private negotiated process. If such Authorized Officer so determines that a negotiated process is most advantageous, any of the Authorized Officers is further authorized to select one or more of such policies based upon a determination of what is in the best interest of the Authority and, regardless of the manner of selection, to negotiate and execute all required agreements and certificates with such selected insurer(s), such agreements and certificates to be in a form acceptable to the General Counsel of the Authority. 19 

SECTION 22. Authorization of Hedge Agreements. The Authorized Officers are each hereby authorized to execute and deliver from time to time one or more agreements or documents with respect to the Future Sales Tax Bonds that will have the benefit of providing the Authority: a guaranteed interest rate, interest rate basis, cash flow basis or purchase price (including, without limitation, agreements or contracts commonly known as interest rate swap, collar cap, or derivative agreements, forward payment conversion agreements, interest rate locks, forward bond purchase agreements, bond warrant agreements or bond purchase option agreements and including agreements or contracts providing for payments based on levels of or changes in interest rates, including a change in an interest rate index, to exchange cash flows or a series of payments, or to hedge payment, rate spread, or similar exposure) as provided in Section 7 of the Bond Authorization Act. Any of the Authorized Officers is authorized to request one or more of the financial advisors to solicit proposals from qualified financial institutions to act as counterparties under one or more of such contracts or agreements. The Board hereby determines that competitive bidding for such contracts or agreements is not required under Section 1.4B of the Chicago Transit Authority Procurement Policy and Procedures inasmuch as the services required are for a professional services, or require technical or artistic skill, and federal funds are not utilized and, as a result, any of the Authorized Officers is authorized to determine whether under then current market conditions it is most advantageous to the Authority to select one or more of such contracts, agreements or counterparties pursuant to a competitive process or a private negotiated process. If such Authorized Officer so determines that a negotiated process is most advantageous, any of the Authorized Officers is further authorized to select one or more of such contracts, agreements and counterparties based upon a determination of what is in the best interest of the Authority and to negotiate and execute all required agreements and certificates with such selected financial institution(s). The stated aggregate notional amount under all such agreements authorized hereunder shall not exceed the principal amount of the series of Future Sales Tax Bonds subject to such hedging agreements (net of offsetting transactions entered into by the Authority). Any such agreement to the extent practicable shall be in substantially the form of either the Local Currency – Single Jurisdiction version or the Multicurrency – Cross Border version of the 1992 ISDA Master Agreement accompanied by the U.S. Municipal Counterparty Schedule published by the International Swaps and Derivatives Association, Inc. (the “ISDA”) or any successor form to either published by the ISDA, with the appropriate confirmations of transactions governed by that agreement, and with such insertions, completions and modifications thereof as shall be approved by an Authorized Officer executing the same, his or her execution to constitute conclusive evidence of the Board’s approval of such insertions, completions and modifications thereof. Should the ISDA form not be the appropriate form to accomplish the objectives of the Authority under this Section, then such other agreement as may be appropriate and in a form acceptable to the General Counsel to the Authority is hereby approved, the execution by any Authorized Officer being conclusive evidence of the Board’s approval of such form. Payments made by 20 

the Authority and payments received by the Authority under such agreements may be paid from and deposited into such funds and accounts as provided in the Indenture and, to the extent provided in the 2010 Indenture or the 2017 Indenture (as applicable), such agreements may constitute Parity Obligations under the 2010 Indenture or Second Lien Parity Obligations under the 2017 Indenture (as applicable). 

SECTION 23. Authorization of Credit Facility Agreements. The Authorized Officers are each hereby authorized to obtain from time to time one or more letters of credit, lines of credit, standby bond purchase agreements or similar credit or liquidity facilities (a “Credit Facility”) with one or more financial institutions with respect to the Future Sales Tax Bonds. Authorized Officers are hereby authorized to enter into a reimbursement agreement and/or standby bond purchase agreement and to execute and issue a promissory note in connection with the provisions of each Credit Facility. The annual fee paid to any financial institution that provides a Credit Facility with respect to all or a portion of a series of the Future Sales Tax Bonds shall not exceed 3% of the average principal amount of such Future Sales Tax Bonds outstanding during such annual period. Any of the Authorized Officers is further authorized to request one or more of the financial advisors to solicit proposals from qualified financial institutions to act as counterparties under one or more of such contracts or agreements. The Board hereby determines that competitive bidding for such contracts or agreements is not required under Section 1.4B of the Chicago Transit Authority Procurement Policy and Procedures inasmuch as the services required are for a professional services, or require technical or artistic skill, and federal funds are not utilized and, as a result, any of the Authorized Officers is authorized to determine whether, under then current market conditions, it is most advantageous to the Authority to select one or more of such contracts, agreements or counterparties pursuant to a competitive process or a private negotiated process. If such Authorized Officer so determines that a negotiated process is most advantageous, any of the Authorized Officers is further authorized to select one or more of such contracts, agreements and counterparties based upon a determination of what is in the best interest of the Authority and to negotiate and execute all required agreements and certificates with such selected financial institution(s). Payments made by the Authority and payments received by the Authority under such agreements may be paid from and deposited into such funds and accounts as provided in the Indenture and, to the extent provided in the 2010 Indenture or the 2017 Indenture (as applicable), such agreements may constitute Parity Obligations under the 2010 Indenture or Second Lien Parity Obligations under the 2017 Indenture (as applicable). 

SECTION 24. Approval of FFGA. The Authorized Officers are each hereby authorized to execute the FFGA in the form required by the FTA, with such changes as may be approved by any Authorized Officer executing the same, with such execution to constitute conclusive evidence of the approval of such Authorized Officer and the Authority of any and all such changes. 21 

SECTION 25. Approval of CMAQ Grant. The Authorized Officers are each hereby authorized to execute the CMAQ Grant, in the form required by the grantor, with such changes as may be approved by any Authorized Officer executing the same, with such execution to constitute conclusive evidence of the approval of such Authorized Officer and the Authority of any and all such changes. 

SECTION 26. Approval of Intergovernmental Agreeement. The Authorized Officers are each hereby authorized to execute and deliver the IGA in the name and on behalf of the Authority on substantially the terms set forth in the draft IGA attached hereto as Exhibit A , with such changes as may be approved by any Authorized Officer executing the same, with such execution to constitute conclusive evidence of the approval of such Authorized Officer and the Authority of any and all such changes. 

SECTION 27. Annual Reporting on the RPM Plan of Finance. The President or designees shall annually report to the Board on the status of implementation of the RPM Plan of Finance, specifically including the accomplishment of the various elements of the RPM Plan of Finance described in this Ordinance. 

SECTION 28. Prior Actions Ratified and Confirmed. The prior actions of the Authorized Officers and all other authorized officers and agents of the Authority in doing any and all acts necessary in connection with the issuance of the RPM TIFIA Bonds and the issuance and sale of the Future Sales Tax Bonds, the execution of the FFGA, the execution of the CMAQ Grant, and the execution of the IGA are hereby approved, ratified and confirmed. 

SECTION 29. Ratification and Continued Effectiveness of Actions of any Authorized Officer Who, for any Reason, Ceases to be an Authorized Officer. In the event that any Authorized Officer executes or delivers any document or other instrument approved hereunder and later ceases to be such an Authorized Officer before the delivery or performance of the document or instrument so executed, whether by reason of resignation, death or otherwise, any such document or instrument so executed or delivered and any such other action taken in connection therewith shall be and continue to be authorized by this ordinance and valid, binding and enforceable against the Authority and the Board. 

SECTION 30. Authorization and Ratification of Subsequent Acts. The Authorized Officers are each hereby authorized to do all such acts and showings and to execute and deliver or accept all such instruments or documents on behalf of the Authority as may be deemed necessary or appropriate to carry out and comply, or evidence compliance with, the provisions of this ordinance, the TIFIA Master Trust Indenture, the TIFIA Supplemental Indenture, the RPM TIFIA Loan Agreement, the 2010 Indenture, the 2017 Indenture, the Sales Tax Supplemental Indentures, the FFGA, the CMAQ Grant, and the IGA, and any other related agreement, including any term sheet or 22 

custody agreement, and all of the acts and doings of the Authorized Officers of the Authority which are in conformity with the intent and purposes of this Ordinance, whether heretofore or hereafter taken or done, shall be and are hereby in all respects, ratified, confirmed and approved. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the Authorized Officers of the Authority are hereby each also authorized to execute, acknowledge and deliver such certificates, agreements and documents which, in the opinion of counsel to the Authority, are necessary to effectuate the provisions of this Ordinance, including the issuance of the RPM TIFIA Bonds, the issuance and sale of the Future Sales Tax Bonds, the execution and delivery of the FFGA, the execution and delivery of the CMAQ Grant, or the execution and delivery of the IGA. 

SECTION 31. Conflicting Ordinances Amended. All other ordinances or parts thereof in conflict herewith are, to the extent of such conflict, hereby amended to conform to this Ordinance. 

SECTION 32. Severability. If any section, paragraph or provision of this Ordinance shall be held invalid or unenforceable for any reason, the invalidity or unenforceability of such section, paragraph or provision shall not affect any remaining provisions. 

SECTION 33. Effective Date; Termination of Effectiveness. This Ordinance shall be in full force and effect from and after its passage and through and including December 31, 2027. The authority delegated to the Authorized Officers pursuant to this Ordinance with respect to the negotiation of the TIFIA Loan, the issuance and delivery of the RPM TIFIA Bonds, the issuance and sale of the Future Sales Tax Bonds, the execution of the FFGA, the execution of the CMAQ Grant and the execution of the IGA shall terminate on December 31, 2027.
